issues: The 'Transformer' node uses a GCP power icon (A7 Power), which is semantically unrelated to a Transformer/LLM and looks like a cloud infrastructure component, not an academic architecture element.
The 'RNN' node uses a network antenna icon, which suggests wireless communication rather than a recurrent neural network; this is misleading in a formal language theory context.
The 'Finite Automaton' node uses a Veeam failover orchestration icon, which is a proprietary IT operations symbol with no relation to automata theory.
The 'Language Family' node uses an AWS Data Set icon, which is a cloud service icon and visually inconsistent with the academic-minimal style requested.
The 'Verification Problem' node uses a gavel icon, which is a legal metaphor and may be acceptable, but it clashes with the otherwise technical iconography.
The legend is placed outside the main flow and duplicates information already conveyed by labels and colors, adding visual clutter.
The annotation 'exponentially more succinct' is placed under the Transformer node but may be ambiguous without an explicit arrow or bracket linking it to the node.
The edge labels 'decides' are repeated on all four edges to the Verification Problem; this is redundant and could be simplified with a single annotation or omitted.
The group 'Equivalent Representations' contains four nodes with very different icon styles (power, formula, antenna, failover), breaking visual consistency.
The diagram uses five distinct icon families (AWS, GCP, Fluent UI, networks2, Veeam, Font Awesome), violating the 'one visual language' requirement.
The 'Language Family' node is positioned above the group boundary, which may cause edge routing to cross the group border awkwardly.
The 'Verification Problem' node is centered but the four incoming edges from widely spaced nodes may create unnecessary crossings or clutter.
The annotation text sizes and colors vary (blue for Transformer, gray for others), which may imply unintended hierarchy.
The 'Consequences' group is visually separated by a red dashed border, but the red color is also used for edges, potentially confusing group semantics with edge semantics.
The diagram lacks explicit indication of the succinctness hierarchy (e.g., size ordering or relative compactness), which is the core message of the prompt.

icon_feedback.why: AWS Data Set icon is a cloud service symbol, not a mathematical set or language family; use a simple circle or rounded rectangle with a label, or a generic set notation symbol.
GCP A7 Power icon is a power/energy symbol, unrelated to Transformer architecture; use a simple rectangle with 'T' or a neural network layer icon, or no icon at all.
Math Formula icon from Fluent UI is appropriate for a logical formula representation, though it could be simplified to a plain rectangle with 'φ' for a more academic look.
Antenna icon implies wireless communication, not a recurrent neural network; use a simple rectangle with 'RNN' or a generic network node icon.
Veeam failover orchestration icon is a proprietary IT operations symbol, completely unrelated to finite automata; use a simple circle or state diagram icon.
Gavel icon is a reasonable metaphor for verification/decision, but consider a checkmark or shield icon for a more technical academic style.
